title: dpw-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Steven "The Edge" Spector

won.source: The fed's own 23 July 1996 title-lineage sheet: 'Steven "The Edge" Spector 7/21/96 to' (won an 8-man tournament final).

note: No document recording the loss of this title survives; by 1 January 1997 the belt was held by 'Devastator' Mick Morton instead.

title: dpw-1996-world-heavyweight
label: "Devastator" Mick Morton

won.source: First attested as champion in the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter and its own New Year's Bash broadcast (retained over Hollywood, 1 January 1997); no document recovered in this wing's own record shows when or how he won the title from Steven Spector.

note: Booked to defend the title against 'Superstar' Steve Sampson at Broken Hearts, 14 February 1997 (not captured in this wing's own record); by the fed's own 8 March 1997 broadcast, Sampson is billed 'the current DPW World Heavyweight Champion.'

title: dpw-1996-world-heavyweight
label: "Superstar" Steve Sampson

won.source: Booked against champion Mick Morton for Broken Hearts in the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter; the match itself is not captured in this wing's own record, but the fed's own 8 March 1997 broadcast billed him 'the current DPW World Heavyweight Champion,' retaining over Matt Harris.

note: Survived a post-match attack by Captain Midnight (chokeslammed his manager, Adrian Stefani, and powerbombed Sampson through a table) on the same 8 March 1997 broadcast; the belt's later history is not captured in this wing's own served record before the fed's own April 1997 closure.

title: dpw-1996-central-valley
label: Mr. Robinson

won.source: First attested as champion (9-0 entering, 10-0 after) in the fed's own New Year's Bash broadcast, retaining over Tony Coltrane; billed 12-0 in the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter.

note: This wing's own accession digest reports the RSPWF Top 200 crediting him a 32-0 run and a #16 finish for the year; the belt's status at the fed's April 1997 closure is not captured in this wing's own served record.

title: dpw-1996-central-valley
label: Drac "The Raven" Dravin

won.source: The fed's own 23 July 1996 title-lineage sheet: awarded the title for outlasting a 92-minute stand in the same Royal Rumble that crowned the World Heavyweight Champion.

note: Held a second reign 18 April - 30 May 1996 before being stripped after a hospitalization angle; the belt passed through Death and a vacancy before 'Enforcer' Chris Michaels won an 8-man tournament final, 21 July 1996 (all per the same 1996 lineage sheet). No document recording the loss of Michaels's reign survives; by 31 January 1997 the belt was held by Mr. Robinson instead.

title: dpw-1996-skyweight
label: Dan James

won.source: First attested as champion in the fed's own New Year's Bash broadcast, defending against King Cobra; this wing's own read of the match does not reach a recorded fall.

note: Neither combatant is minted as a character in this wing (each falls short of the 2-served-appearance threshold); the belt's outcome after 1 January 1997 is not captured in this wing's own served record.

title: dpw-1996-skyweight
label: The Hitman

won.source: The fed's own 23 July 1996 title-lineage sheet: 'Hitman 7/21/96 to'.

note: No document recording the loss of this title survives; by 1 January 1997 the belt was held by Dan James instead.

title: dpw-1996-network
label: Daemon "The Dragon" Dempsey

won.source: First attested as champion in the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter (10-4-5).

note: No document recording the loss of this title survives; by the fed's own 8 March 1997 broadcast, Hollywood was again billed 'the current Network Champion,' with Dempsey himself appearing that night to call out the new challenger, The Boogieman.

title: dpw-1996-network
label: Hollywood

won.source: The fed's own Motor City Madness table of contents: won a 16-man 'Rage in the Cage' tournament for the title.

note: No document recording the loss of this title survives; by 31 January 1997 the belt was held by Daemon 'The Dragon' Dempsey instead.

title: dpw-1996-network
label: Hollywood [2]

won.source: Billed 'the current Network Champion' in the fed's own 8 March 1997 broadcast, defending against The Boogieman.

note: This wing's own read of the 8 March 1997 broadcast reaches a post-match beatdown of The Boogieman by an unidentified trio but not a confirmed pinfall; the defense's outcome and the title's status at the fed's April 1997 closure are not asserted here.

title: dpw-1996-world-tag-team
label: The New Negaforce

won.source: First attested as champions in the fed's own 31 January 1997 newsletter (3-0); the team is seen defeating Extreme Justice on the fed's own New Year's Bash broadcast, 1 January 1997, though that match is not billed as a title defense in the text.

note: The belts' status at the fed's April 1997 closure is not captured in this wing's own served record.

title: dpw-1996-world-tag-team
label: Hardcore Heaven

won.source: The fed's own 23 July 1996 title-lineage sheet: 'Hardcore Heaven 7/21/96 to'.

note: No document recording the loss of this title survives; by 31 January 1997 the belts were held by The New Negaforce instead. The fed's own New Year's Bash preview commentary (not independently served in this wing) names an intervening challenger, Milky Cereal, defending against the King's Men -- neither team minted here.
